anomalies.observed: The PCA9685PW PWM driver (U2) has its address pins A0-A5 (pins 1-6) all tied to GND, which sets its I2C address to 0x40. The INA219 current sensor (U1) also has its address pins A0 and A1 tied to GND, setting it to 0x40. Both devices share the same I2C2 bus. A text note next to U2 says 'I2C address: 0x41', contradicting the pin strapping.
anomalies.expected: To avoid an address conflict on the shared I2C2 bus, the PCA9685 should be set to 0x41 (e.g. by tying A0 to +3.3V) while the INA219 remains at 0x40, or the INA219 should be moved to a different address. The specification lists both devices at 0x40, which is a conflict.

anomalies.impact: Both the INA219 and PCA9685 will respond to the same I2C address on the same bus, causing bus contention and preventing reliable communication with either device.

anomalies.observed: The USB D+ and D- pins of the CH330 USB-UART bridges (U11, U12) are connected to the same nets (USB_DP_FCC/USB_DM_FCC and USB_DP_NAVC/USB_DM_NAVC) as the STM32 MCU USB pins and the USB connectors (USB1, USB2). No multiplexer, switch, or jumper separates the two USB devices.
anomalies.expected: The MCU USB interface and the CH330 USB interface should not share the same USB data lines simultaneously. Either separate USB connectors, a multiplexer, or isolation jumpers are required to select between the MCU USB (DFU) and the USB-UART bridge.

evidence.quote: Connections sheet, USB Debug block: U11 pin3 (D+) connects to net USB_DP_FCC; USB1 pin3 (D+) connects to USB_DP_FCC through R52.
FCC sheet: FCC1 PA11 (pin70) = USB_DM_FCC, PA12 (pin71) = USB_DP_FCC.
programming/debug via SWD, USB DFU, and UART-to-USB

anomalies.impact: When a USB cable is connected, both the STM32 USB peripheral and the CH330 will attempt to enumerate on the same bus, leading to bus contention and likely failure of USB communication for both debug and DFU modes.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a likely I2C address conflict between the PCA9685 PWM driver and the INA219 current sensor (both set to 0x40 on the same bus), and a USB data line conflict where the CH330 USB-UART bridges are hardwired in parallel with the STM32 USB pins without any selection mechanism.
